title: Ditwah relief for Army personnel
byline: Welfare vouchers worth over Rs. 26 million were distributed among Sri Lanka Army personnel affected by the Ditwah cyclone at a special programme held at Army Headquarters.

title: Iran delegation arrives in Pakistan for US talks
byline: Pakistan has confirmed the arrival of a senior Iranian delegation in Islamabad ahead of expected negotiations with the United States. According to Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the delegation — led by Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf — was received by Ishaq Dar and other senior officials.

title: NASA’s Artemis II crew splashes down after history-making moon mission
byline: The Artemis II, and the four astronauts aboard the Orion space capsule, has splashed down into the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, Nasa has confirmed.

title: Iran’s parliament speaker says negotiations can’t start without Lebanon ceasefire
byline: Al Jazeera- Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said negotiations with the US cannot begin until two key conditions are met: the implementation of a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of frozen Iranian assets.

title: Suspected Sri Lankan overstayer caught in ICA operation while sleeping at HDB rooftop garden
byline: The man was sleeping in a garden above an HDB multi-storey carpark in Woodlands when plainclothes officers surrounded him during a pre-dawn operation on April 8.

title: NDA candidates booked after Sri Lankan diplomat joins fishermen interaction in Puducherry
byline: A case has been registered against two Indian National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidates in India’s Puducherry based on a complaint by the Returning Officer, following allegations of violating the election code of conduct during a fishermen’s meeting attended by Sri Lanka’s Deputy Consul General for South India, Ganesanathan Ketheeswaran.

title: Fire erupts at Karadiyana garbage dump; Residents advised to wear face masks
byline: A sudden fire broke out this evening at the Karadiyana waste management site in Piliyandala. Police said the blaze has sent thick plumes of smoke across the area.

title: Vance departs for talks in Pakistan, as Israel bombs Lebanon
byline: US Vice President JD Vance has departed for Islamabad, where he is scheduled to join talks with Iran on Saturday to end their war.

title: Presidential Commission to probe coal purchase deals
byline: A commission comprising sitting judges will be appointed to probe the coal procurement deals that had taken place since the commissioning of the Norochcholai Power Plant, Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake told Parliament today.

title: Lebanon says ceasefire must be in place before Israel talks
byline: A senior official in the Lebanese president’s office has told the BBC that Lebanon will participate in direct negotiations with Israel next week only if there is a ceasefire in place beforehand.

title: No faith motion against Power and Energy Minister defeated
byline: The no faith motion against Minister of Power and Energy Kumara Jayakody was defeated by a majority of 104 votes with 43 MPs voting in favour and 153  against. Some 22 MPs were absent during the time of voting.

title: CSE rallies strongly on renewed investor confidence and broad-based buying
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed on a strong and optimistic note on 10th April 2026, reflecting renewed confidence in both domestic economic conditions and improving global sentiment. From the opening bell, the market maintained steady upward momentum, driven by broad-based buying interest across multiple sectors.

title: China-funded school uniform distribution completed for 2026
byline: The distribution of school uniform fabric provided as a grant by the People’s Republic of China for the year 2026 has been successfully completed, the Education Ministry announced.

title: Purchase energy efficient electrical appliances for New Year:  Sustainable Energy Authority
byline: The Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority urged the people to purchase high-energy efficient electrical appliances in the New Year, considering the energy crisis faced by the country.

title: Ranil taken to Singapore for medical care as CID is after doctors treating him here: Wajira
byline: The United National Party (UNP) said that its leader and former President Ranil Wickremesinghe had to be taken to Singapore for medical treatment because the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) was on a witch-hunt against Sri Lankan doctors who treated him.

title: March Mahapola scholarship Rs. 10,000 credited to student accounts
byline: The Mahapola Scholarship installment for March has been credited to university students’ bank accounts today (10), the Lalith Athulathmudali Mahapola Higher Education Scholarship Trust Fund (MTF) said.

title: Three arrested over Rs. 30 million Canada job scam
byline: Three individuals have been arrested over an alleged large-scale job scam involving nearly Rs. 30 million, where victims were promised employment opportunities in Canada, the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) said.

title: Lufthansa flights disrupted as cabin crew stage strike
byline: Lufthansa (LHAG.DE), flights were significantly disrupted on Friday as cabin crew union UFO staged a one-day strike, the airline’s third ​work stoppage in two months, impacting operations at its ‌Frankfurt and Munich hubs.

title: Spanish minister urges Iran to negotiate in ‘good faith’
byline: Spain’s Foreign Minister has told reporters before Saturday’s talks: “I encourage Iran, this is what I conveyed to the Iranian foreign minister, to take part in those negotiations and to participate in good faith.”

title: Day after National Vesak Festival not a public holiday: Labour Dept.
byline: The Labour Department has clarified that the day after the National Vesak Festival in 2026, which falls on May 30, will not be observed as a public holiday.

title: Severe lightning warning issued for several provinces
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued a warning for Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, and Uva provinces, as well as Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts, stating that thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several locations after 1.00 p.m.

title: France and Pakistan condemn ‘Lebanon ceasefire violations’
byline: Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot have “expressed concern over serious ceasefire violations made in Lebanon”, in a phone call on Friday morning.

title: Health sector heading for crisis due to multiple challenges: Doctors’ Union
byline: The Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights has warned that Sri Lanka’s health sector is heading towards a serious crisis due to multiple challenges, including shortages of doctors and other healthcare personnel, lack of essential equipment, poor maintenance, and insufficient raw materials for laboratory and other services.

title: Iran’s former foreign minister Kamal Kharrazi dies following Israeli strike on home
byline: Kamal Kharrazi, Iran’s former foreign minister and head of the Strategic Council on Foreign Relations, died on the evening of April 10 from injuries sustained in a US-Israeli strike on his home, Eqtesad Online reported.

title: Navy seizes Indian trawler, 10 fishermen held off Mannar
byline: Ten Indian fishermen were apprehended while allegedly poaching in Sri Lankan waters north of Mannar.

title: India proposes new rules to regulate news and political posts on social media
byline: The Indian government has proposed changes to extend its regulatory framework to a wider range of online news voices, including influencers and podcasters on platforms such as Facebook, YouTube and X.

title: IRD records Rs. 606 bn revenue in first quarter of 2026
byline: The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) has collected tax revenue amounting to Rs. 606,002 million during the first quarter of 2026, continuing its strong performance following a record-breaking year in 2025.

title: Colombo Central Bus Stand damage may be organised act: Deputy Minister
byline: Damage caused to sanitary facilities at the newly renovated Colombo Central Bus Stand may be the result of an organised activity, Transport and Highways Deputy Minister M.M. Prasanna Kumara Gunasena said.

title: Netanyahu faces domestic and international pressure
byline: Polls released in the Israeli media are pointing out what a difficult position Benjamin Netanyahu is in.

title: Vijay’s unreleased film Jana Nayagan leaked online before TN polls
byline: Tamil superstar Vijay’s final film, Jana Nayagan, has been leaked online, even though it hasn’t been released in theatres yet. On Thursday night, small clips from the film were shared on social media, and by Friday morning, HD prints of the full film were uploaded to piracy sites. The unreleased film has yet to receive CBFC clearance and has been in limbo for three months.

title: Passenger arrested at BIA with illegal ornamental plants worth Rs. 775,000
byline: A 40-year-old Sri Lankan businessman was arrested by Customs officers at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) this morning (11) for attempting to smuggle a consignment of ornamental plants valued at Rs. 775,000.

title: No shortage of fertilizer; stocks exceed requirement: Deputy Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Namal Karunaratne today (11) assured that there is no shortage of fertilizer in the country, stating that current stocks exceed the required levels for cultivation.

title: GMOA ends 48-hour token strike, future action to be decided after New Year
byline: The Government Medical Officers Association (GMOA) announced that its 48-hour token strike concluded at 8.00 a.m. today (11), restoring normal hospital services across the country.

title: Heavy New Year travel rush at Makumbura
byline: A surge of passengers was reported at the Makumbura Multimodal Centre (MMC) this morning (11) as commuters began travelling to their hometowns for the upcoming Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Kabir appointed SJB Chairman
byline: MP Kabir Hashim has been appointed as the Chairman of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), the Opposition Leader’s Office said today.

title: Trump praises Artemis II crew, hints at future Mars mission
byline: Donald Trump praised the crew of Artemis II after they safely returned to Earth, calling the mission “spectacular” and the landing “perfect.”

title: Mahinda Rajapaksa submits assets affidavit to Bribery Commission
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa has submitted a sworn affidavit to the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC), declaring his assets, expenditures, and sources of income.

title: China assures uninterrupted fuel supply to Sri Lanka amid Middle East tensions
byline: Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Qi Zhenhong said there will be no fuel shortage in Sri Lanka, assuring continued support from China despite global uncertainties linked to the Middle East crisis.

title: ‘Strait of Hormuz will open, with or without Iran’: Donald Trump ahead of peace talks in Pakistan
byline: US President Donald Trump on Friday (local time) asserted the Strait of Hormuz “will open with or without Iran,” ahead of ceasefire talks with Tehran scheduled in Islamabad.

title: Take hard line on doctors’ strikes: Kananathan
byline: Former diplomat Ambassador Kananathan has called on the government to take a firm stance on doctors’ strikes, warning that Sri Lanka has reached a critical moment.

title: Police on high alert over drugs hidden in children’s toys
byline: Police have been placed on high alert following a disturbing trend in which drug traffickers are using children’s toys to conceal and transport illegal narcotics through courier services, the Daily Mirror learns.

title: EU airline industry warns of fuel shortages if Strait of Hormuz stays closed
byline: Europe will suffer jet fuel shortages in just three weeks if the the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen, the trade body for the continent’s airports has warned.

title: Summon Central Bank officials before Privileges Committee: MP
byline: Accusing Central Bank officials of continued unilateral conduct, opacity, arrogance or ignorance, and an apparent disregard for parliamentary accountability, Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake yesterday called for the summoning of Central Bank officials before the Parliamentary Committee on Privileges.

title: Inaction of CB has led to NDB scam: Ravi K
byline: The complete failure of the Banking Supervisory Unit of the Central Bank (CB) has led to the Rs. 13 billion scam at the NDB which has become more complex today, MP Ravi Karunanayake said today.

title: CPC suspends QR fuel quotas for festive season
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has announced a temporary suspension of the QR-based fuel quota system for petrol vehicles, effective from today (April 11) until April 18, 2026.

title: Crude oil prices decline
byline: Brent crude oil prices on Saturday eased as Iranian and United States delegations head to Islamabad for the peace talks. The decline in crude prices is giving hope to consumers after oil prices dipped before reaching a record of $119 per barrel during the recent tensions in the Middle East.

title: Group of schoolchildren consuming liquor arrested
byline: A group of schoolchildren from a leading school in the Haldumulla area were arrested yesterday for consuming liquor during school hours. All of them were about 16 years of age.

title: US plane carrying team for talks with Iran lands in Islamabad
byline: A U.S. government plane ​carrying top U.S. ‌officials landed in the Pakistani capital ​Islamabad on ​Saturday for peace talks with ⁠Iran, two ​Pakistani sources told ​Reuters.

title: Chinese national arrested at BIA with Rs. 3.9 million cigarette consignment
byline: A 35-year-old Chinese businessman was arrested by Customs officers at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) this morning (11) for attempting to smuggle a consignment of cigarettes valued at Rs. 3,915,000.

title: Fake driver’s license racket uncovered at Werahera DMT
byline: Police have uncovered a racket involving the issuance of counterfeit driver’s licenses targeting individuals visiting the Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) in Werahera.

title: Sun overhead at 12:11 p.m. today in Anuradhapura and several areas
byline: The sun will be directly overhead today (11) at around 12:11 p.m. in areas including Pomparippu, Anuradhapura, Mihintale, Galenbindunuwewa, Agbopura and Serunuwara, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Trump praises Artemis II crew, hints at future Mars mission
byline: Donald Trump praised the crew of Artemis II after they safely returned to Earth, calling the mission “spectacular” and the landing “perfect.”

title: ‘Strait of Hormuz will open, with or without Iran’: Donald Trump ahead of peace talks in Pakistan
byline: US President Donald Trump on Friday (local time) asserted the Strait of Hormuz “will open with or without Iran,” ahead of ceasefire talks with Tehran scheduled in Islamabad.

title: Maldives President to visit Sri Lanka
byline: The President of the Maldives, Mohamed Muizzu, is scheduled to visit Sri Lanka next month, with discussions already underway to strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in the fisheries sector.

title: Iran’s new supreme leader has severe and disfiguring wounds, sources say
byline: Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is still recovering from severe facial and leg injuries suffered in the airstrike that killed his father at the beginning of the war, three people close to his inner circle told Reuters.

title: Iran leader says US should focus on ‘America First’ policy – not ‘Israel First’
byline: Iran’s first vice president says the outcome of the high-stakes negotiations in Islamabad rests entirely on US priorities.

title: Secretary to President complains to CID over coal imports
byline: The Secretary to the President has lodged a complaint with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) requesting a formal investigation into coal imports since 2009.

title: Iran has lost track of mines it planted in Hormuz, reopening delayed: Report
byline: Iran’s inability to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz stems from a basic problem that it cannot locate all the naval mines it deployed during the Middle East conflict and lacks the technical capability to remove them, US officials told The New York Times.

title: Hormuz remains at near standstill after ceasefire
byline: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained well below normal volumes despite a U.S.-Iran ceasefire as Tehran asserted its control by warning ships to keep to its territorial waters while doing so.

title: UK-Based Entrepreneur and Jaffna College Alumnus donates Rs. 30M bus in memory of mother
byline: Seevaratnam Muresh, UK-based entrepreneur, a proud Old Boy of Jaffna College, Vaddukoddai, and current President of the Jaffna College Alumni Association UK, donated a brand-new Rs. 30 million Mitsubishi Fuso bus to the college. The bus was officially handed over to the Principal, Rushira Kulasingam, on February 27, 2026, in loving memory of his late mother, Thirumalar, on the first anniversary of her passing.

title: Gap between rich and poor nations growing even wider: UN report
byline: The gap between rich and poor nations is widening as key reforms promised last year, including changes to global financial institutions, remain largely unimplemented, a new UN report has warned.

title: No fines collected on substandard eye medicines, says doctors’ union
byline: The Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights, claimed that no fines have been collected so far from pharmaceutical companies accused of importing substandard eye medicines and other drugs into the country.

title: Wildlife Department employee killed by elephant
byline: An employee of the Wildlife Conservation Department assigned for duty in the Wanathawilluwa-Thewanuwara electric fence had been trampled to death by a rogue elephant on his way back after duty.

title: EU airline industry warns of fuel shortages if Strait of Hormuz stays closed
byline: Europe will suffer jet fuel shortages in just three weeks if the the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen, the trade body for the continent’s airports has warned.
